Hi Tom / Acme implementation team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate you walking through the current search flow and the priority metrics for product pages (CTR, add-to-cart rate, and search-to-purchase). As discussed, this thread will capture the execution plan for the embeddings + rerank cutover and the specific responsibilities for Red- and Acme-side teams.

High level asks / goals:
- Finalize backfill window and DB target by EOD Friday (helps us reserve dedicated pool).
- Run rerank evals on holdout queries and bake-in thresholds for rollout (precision@5 and click-through lift targets).
- Execute a staged cutover with canary (1% traffic) then 10%/50%/100% ramps and automated rollback on quality regression.

Proposed immediate schedule (subject to your confirmation):
1) Wed 6/30: finalize vector DB target + agree backfill window
2) Thu 7/1: preflight smoke on staging; share rerank eval spec; load small seed index
3) Fri 7/2: full backfill (estimated 6-8 hrs), run rerank evals on fresh index
4) Mon 7/5: canary production 1% -> evaluate for 24h -> ramp per MAP

Open questions we need from Acme before Friday:
- Do you prefer Pinecone or Redis Enterprise for the primary store? (you mentioned an internal tilt toward managed Pinecone if cost acceptable)
- Any blackout windows for the ecom stack (deploy freeze)?

Attachments for your review: acme-backfill-window-proposal.xlsx (workload estimates), embed-backfill-checklist.csv (backfill steps), rerank-eval-spec.md (metrics and eval queries).

Thanks — I’ll wait for Tom’s confirmation on DB choice and freeze windows, then Marissa will kick off the staging smoke.

—

Thanks Tom — Pinecone works for us. Quick notes from engineering on compatibility and the staging checklist:

- Bulk backfill approach: we will use a checkpointed pipeline that upserts in 100k batches with retry and idempotency markers; pipeline supports resume on failure. See embed-backfill-checklist.csv for concrete steps.
- Estimated throughput into Pinecone (m5-large-ish client): ~45k vectors/hour per worker; parallelize across 6 workers -> ~270k/hr. Your dataset (~1.2M records) should backfill in ~5 hours excluding pre-processing. Add 20% buffer for embedding generation.
- Preflight smoke: Marissa (me) will run a 10k record seed load into a staging index and run a scripted rerank evaluation; I'll post results and any divergence flags to the MAP doc.
- Rerank eval spec: Ben attached a draft; short version: precision@5, ndcg@10, and relative CTR lift on production logs mapped to holdout queries. We will also run qualitative checklists on top queries (search result correctness).

Marissa
Engineering Program Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Folks — adding technical details and the quick decision matrix we discussed for vector store selection and rollout knobs. Attaching rerank-eval-spec.md and a short backfill checklist. Key points below: 

- Vector store selection: Pinecone (managed) is fine; ensure namespace isolation per environment (staging/prod) to avoid accidental reads. For long term, consider a Redis-based cache layer for hot shards if you need sub-20ms tail latency.
- Embedding generation: we recommend batching at token level to avoid small requests; use Redwood SDK bulk endpoints with 8–16k token windows.
- Backfill safety: run backfill to a new index name with timestamped suffix, validate eval metrics against holdout; only swap alias to new index after smoke and rollback window closes.
- Rerank evals: we will run both automated metric checks and a human sample of top 50 queries. Thresholds: precision@5 >= baseline+6%, ndcg@10 >= baseline+4%, and CTR uplift >= +3% relative to baseline within 24h of canary. If any threshold fails we will not proceed with ramp.

Attachments referenced: rerank-eval-spec.md, embed-backfill-checklist.csv (see drive link in MAP).

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
